theme: The inventor's workshop: a maker who switches between a jeweller's loupe and a spyglass, the finest detail and the far horizon, and who takes everything apart to find out why it works.
cast: THE MAKER, the recurring hero: a small, round, fuzzy creature with huge, slightly mismatched round eyes, a jeweller's loupe screwed into one eye, a battered brass spyglass tucked under one arm, a single curly antenna-like tuft of hair on top of his head, patched dungarees and a tool belt stuffed with pencils, screwdrivers and a tiny hammer; endlessly curious, delighted and a little obsessive. THE SIDEKICK (only where the subject asks for him): a scrappy, hand-built little robot made of tin cans and a dented kettle, with a bendy desk lamp for a head that glows, riveted patches and mismatched bolt eyes; eager, helpful and a little clumsy. THE TOWNSFOLK: tall, solemn, slightly droopy creatures in bowler hats and long buttoned coats, mostly bemused or astonished by the maker.

images.name: the-pancake-machine
images.subject: A simple, uncluttered scene with lots of empty white paper around it. The maker, large and clearly visible from the front in the centre, grins with delight as he pedals a little bicycle bolted to a homemade pancake-flipping machine: the pedals turn a chain and a big gear, which swings a spring-loaded wooden arm with a spatula on the end. The arm has just flung a pancake high out of a frying pan on a small camping stove, the pancake flipping mid-air with motion lines and a puff of steam. On the right, the tin-can robot sidekick, its desk-lamp head tilted up and eyes wide, holds out a plate with a tall, wobbly stack of pancakes to catch it. A jug of batter and a pat of butter sit on a crate. Only these elements; no crowd, no background buildings.
images.alt: A grinning fuzzy maker pedals a homemade machine that flips a pancake high out of a frying pan, while a tin-can robot holds out a plate with a tall stack of pancakes to catch it.

images.name: why-it-ticks
images.subject: In the maker's workshop, a cuckoo clock that a townsperson brought in to be fixed has been completely taken apart: hundreds of gears, springs, screws, the little cuckoo bird and the pendulum laid out in tidy rows across a long workbench and onto the floor. The maker holds up a single tiny spring with tweezers right in front of his loupe, eyes enormous with wonder. Behind him the tall townsperson in a bowler hat still waits, holding a teacup, deadpan, while a spider has spun a cobweb between the brim of their hat and their shoulder. The empty clock case hangs on the wall.
images.alt: A maker has taken a cuckoo clock apart into hundreds of neatly laid-out pieces and gazes in wonder at one tiny spring, while its owner waits with a teacup and a cobweb grows on their hat.

images.name: off-the-instructions
images.after: I was [building Figma plugins with AI]
images.subject: On one side, a long shelf of identical little toy cars, each sitting neatly on its kit box whose picture shows exactly that car. In the middle, the maker and the tin-can robot sidekick have built the very same kit into a towering, joyful contraption: the little toy car is still at its base, but it now carries a patchwork sail, a crane, a propeller, a periscope, extra wheels and two small rockets, with smoke puffing out. The robot holds the other end of a huge wrench; the maker sits at the top, tightening a final bolt. The kit's instruction leaflet drifts away on the wind, ignored. Two townsfolk gape at it, one dropping their hat.
images.alt: Beside a shelf of identical toy cars built exactly as their boxes show, a maker and a tin-can robot have built the same kit into a towering contraption with a sail, crane and rockets.

images.name: weeds-and-horizon
images.after: For me, these aren't separate ways of thinking.
images.subject: PANEL 1: deep in the cramped engine room of a little steam ship, among tangled pipes and overgrown weeds, the maker crouches with his loupe and finds one cracked cog among many. PANEL 2: the maker has climbed to the top of the ship's mast with his spyglass and sees that the ship is heading straight for a gloomy, rocky island; he points urgently the other way, towards a bright island with a lighthouse. PANEL 3: back in the engine room, the maker ignores a heap of shiny but useless parts and replaces just that one cracked cog; through the porthole behind him, the ship has turned and is now sailing towards the bright island.
images.alt: A three-panel comic: in a ship's engine room a maker finds one cracked cog; from the mast he sees the ship heading for the wrong island; back below he fixes only that cog and the ship turns for the right one.
